summary:
PARVATI is an AI-powered geospatial platform developed to assess potential Glacial Lake Outburst Flood (GLOF) risks in the Himalayan region. It integrates satellite imagery, glacier inventories, digital elevation models, historical GLOF records, and geographical datasets to analyse glacier movement, glacial lake characteristics, terrain susceptibility, and downstream exposure.

The platform uses geospatial processing and machine-learning techniques, including Random Forest, K-Means clustering, and Isolation Forest, to identify spatial patterns and prioritize potentially vulnerable lakes and areas. Its interactive 3D dashboard brings together terrain visualization, glacier monitoring, lake analysis, predictive screening, and hypothetical GLOF scenarios.

By transforming diverse geospatial datasets into an integrated risk-screening and visualization system, PARVATI aims to support researchers and disaster-management authorities in identifying areas requiring further investigation and prioritizing field assessments. It provides a foundation for future development of validated flood simulations and early-warning capabilities.
details:
PARVATI is an integrated geospatial and machine-learning platform developed to assess potential Glacial Lake Outburst Flood (GLOF) risks in the Himalayan region, focusing on Samudra Tapu and Bara Shigri.

How does it work?

The platform integrates multiple datasets, including NISAR SAR imagery, Sentinel-2 optical imagery, Digital Elevation Models (DEM), Randolph Glacier Inventory (RGI), historical GLOF records, ITS_LIVE glacier velocity data, OpenStreetMap, and WorldPop.

These datasets undergo geospatial preprocessing, harmonization, and feature extraction. The system analyses glacier displacement, glacial lake characteristics, terrain elevation, slope, drainage networks, watershed boundaries, and downstream exposure.

Machine-learning techniques, including K-Means clustering, Isolation Forest, anomaly-based spatial screening, and Random Forest classification, are used to identify spatial patterns and prioritize potentially vulnerable lakes and areas. The outputs are integrated into an interactive 3D dashboard featuring terrain visualization, glacier monitoring, lake analysis, predictive analysis, and hypothetical scenario exploration.

Benefits and Intended Impact

  • Helps identify and prioritize potentially vulnerable glacial lakes.
  • Integrates fragmented satellite, terrain, and historical datasets.
  • Supports downstream infrastructure and population exposure assessment.
  • Provides interactive 3D visualization for improved geographical understanding.
  • Supports research, field-survey prioritization, and disaster-risk planning.

Tools and Technologies Used

  • Programming: Python, JavaScript
  • Geospatial processing: Rasterio, GeoPandas, NumPy
  • Machine Learning: Scikit-learn
  • Visualization: React, Three.js, React Three Fiber
  • Data: NISAR, Sentinel-2, DEM, RGI, ITS_LIVE, HMA GLOF Database, OpenStreetMap, WorldPop
  • Data formats: GeoTIFF, GeoJSON, CSV, NetCDF

Creativity and Innovation

PARVATI combines satellite-based glacier monitoring, lake morphology analysis, terrain susceptibility screening, historical GLOF information, and downstream exposure assessment within a unified platform. Its interactive 3D dashboard makes complex geospatial results easier to explore and interpret.

Factors Considered

Our development considered data availability, spatial resolution, coordinate reference systems, temporal consistency, dataset quality, uncertainty, geographical coverage, model validation, and the limitations of historical event records. We also considered the importance of distinguishing potential risk indicators from confirmed flood predictions.
